content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/spec.md).

It defines a private, responsive bookmark manager with:

- Saving and opening bookmarks
- Tags, search, and filtering
- Editing and confirmed deletion
- Duplicate and URL validation
- Persistent user collections
- Keyboard accessibility
- Clear MVP exclusions such as sharing, imports, folders, extensions, and offline use

The quality checklist passed all checks: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/checklists/requirements.md).

Feature directory: `specs/001-manage-bookmarks`

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan; no code has been written yet.

This looks good overall — it covers what I care about most: saving a link, opening it later, tagging, searching and filtering, editing, and deleting with a confirmation so I don't wipe something out by accident. Keeping my bookmarks private and being able to get through everything without a mouse are both fine by me too.

One thing about saving that matters to me: I'd really like to just paste a web address and have the app fill in the page's name for me, instead of typing a title every time. That's the main convenience I was hoping for when saving. I saw you've listed automatic title/icon fetching as out of scope for now — I can live with entering titles myself to get started, but I'd like it noted as something I want soon.

With that understood, the spec is good enough for what I need. Please go ahead and create the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review: [plan.md](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/plan.md).

Key decisions:

- Next.js 16 and TypeScript on Node.js 24
- PostgreSQL with Prisma for private, durable storage
- Better Auth with database-backed email/password sessions
- Server-side search, tag filtering, and pagination
- Database-enforced duplicate and user-isolation rules
- Keyboard-focused UI and browser accessibility tests
- Automatic title retrieval documented as the prioritized post-MVP feature

Supporting design artifacts:

- [Research decisions](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/data-model.md)
- [HTTP contract](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Validation quickstart](/work/specs/001-manage-bookmarks/quickstart.md)

The plan passes its scope, privacy, accessibility, simplicity, and testability gates. No application code or task breakdown has been created yet.

Please approve the plan or request changes. After approval, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered implementation tasks.

I spent some time actually using it, and most of it works nicely. I signed in, saved links with tags, opened my list, searched, filtered by a tag, edited a bookmark, and deleted one — all smooth, and my links stayed put. Trying to save a nonsense address was correctly refused with a clear message. Good work.

One thing is off, and it's exactly the case we agreed on. When I try to save a link that's already in my collection, instead of telling me it's already saved and taking me to the existing one, it shows an error that says the bookmark "could not be saved, please try again." That's confusing — it sounds like something broke and that retrying might work, when really I just already have that link. I tried it with the same address and again with a slightly different capitalization, and both gave that same error.

Please fix that so re-saving a link I already have quietly points me to the existing bookmark rather than showing a failure message. Everything else I tried is working well, so once that duplicate case behaves right, I expect I'll be happy.
